tasks.short: Integrate continuity plans across teams and coordinate their operation during disruptions.

steps.what: Retrieve current plans, recovery requirements and dependency records.
Request changes and readiness confirmations from service owners.
Compare recovery sequences, dependencies and resource commitments across plans.

loop.input: Versioned plans, readiness updates and a structured dependency register.
loop.output: Proposed conflicts with source passages and affected services.
loop.check: Validate service identifiers, references and timing constraints; the planner checks substantive conflicts.
loop.stop: One comparison and one correction pass per plan batch; unresolved conflicts enter the review queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Timing checks are deterministic, but dependencies and commitments also appear in inconsistent prose.

steps.what: Agree recovery priorities and resolve competing resource commitments.
Revise shared procedures, escalation paths and recovery checklists.

loop.input: Approved integration decisions, current procedures and controlled templates.
loop.output: Tracked plan revisions and a change summary.
loop.check: Check required sections and references; reject unsupported instructions and altered recovery targets.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per plan; unresolved passages return to the planner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates assemble the pack, but procedural wording must reflect decisions expressed in free text.

steps.what: Approve the integrated plans and accept outstanding readiness limitations.
Publish approved plans and assign readiness actions.
Coordinate activation and escalate recovery conflicts during a disruption.

tasks.design: A portable register in the {WORKFLOW} links versioned plans in the {DOCS} to dependencies, owners and readiness actions in the {PROJECT}. Deterministic checks flag timing conflicts; bounded model loops propose prose conflicts and tracked revisions with source references. Approval releases each plan, while activation and recovery tradeoffs remain with the incident commander.
tasks.previous_blocker: Plans used inconsistent wording and separate ownership. Keeping dependencies and versions aligned required repeated coordination.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building importers, comparison checks and revision generators. Structured owner confirmations reduce reconciliation work without requiring a new reasoning breakthrough.
tasks.still_hard: Shared recovery resources, uncertain incident information and unavailable services require negotiation. The coordination tools also need an accessible fallback during outages.
tasks.human_edge: The planner secures credible commitments and recognises when a technically consistent plan cannot work under pressure.
tasks.altitude: The week shifts from chasing versions to resolving dependency conflicts and rehearsing recovery choices. The planner can propose cross-service priorities more often; risk acceptance and activation rights remain with designated leaders.

reach.task: Sequence recovery dependencies across technology changes.
reach.learn: Change windows, restoration prerequisites and evidence of successful recovery.
Site access, utilities, occupancy constraints and fallback communications.

evidence.claim: Version control, structured confirmations and dependency checks can support continuity-plan integration deterministically.
Live recovery coordination needs human judgement when information and resource availability change.

assumptions: The pilot covers a small set of critical services and approved file exports.
Time shares describe ordinary integration work; disruption periods can make live coordination dominant.
Service owners still confirm readiness; reminders do not establish readiness.
Build ranges are working-day estimates for a pilot, not a replacement for every recovery system.
Consent and access include permissions and any employee consultation required by national rules; elapsed waiting time may be longer.
GDPR applies to personal contact data; EU AI Act obligations depend on the intended use.
unknowns: Which services and dependencies already have authoritative owners?
Who may approve plans, accept readiness exceptions and authorise activation?
Which exports, interfaces and offline communication channels are available?
Do national rules or existing agreements require employee consultation for the proposed changes?
research_questions: Which dependency conflicts can be detected with explicit timing and capacity rules?
Can the coordination pack remain usable when primary identity, communication or document services fail?
new_work: Review proposed conflicts and unsupported plan revisions.
Maintain service identifiers, dependency rules and approval routes.
Resolve missing owner confirmations and stale source records.
Test offline access and fallback communications.

tasks.short: Build and obtain approval for continuity and disaster recovery budgets.

steps.what: Retrieve actual expenditure, commitments and current budget limits.
Collate quotations and staffing estimates supplied by procurement and service owners.

loop.input: Received quotations and staffing estimates with their dates and source files.
loop.output: Cost assumptions with units, currency, exclusions, validity dates and source references.
loop.check: Validate totals and units; flag missing tax treatment, recurring charges and ambiguous exclusions.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per file; ambiguous entries go to the planner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured submissions need only validation, but received quotations also contain material conditions in prose.

steps.what: Calculate recovery-option costs, cash timing and contingency allowances.
Compare affordability, recovery benefits and residual exposure with service owners and finance.
Prepare the budget proposal and explain assumptions and unfunded requirements.

loop.input: Validated scenario tables, investment priorities and a proposal template.
loop.output: Budget narrative linked to calculated figures and recorded decisions.
loop.check: Insert numbers deterministically; verify every stated benefit and unfunded requirement against approved inputs.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unsupported benefit claims remain blank for human completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Tables use templates, but the rationale must explain case-specific tradeoffs in plain language.

steps.what: Approve funding and accept the stated unfunded recovery requirements.
Record approved budget lines against cost centres and recovery initiatives.

tasks.design: An approved export from the {ERP} feeds a deterministic cost model with versioned assumptions and recovery options. A bounded loop extracts quotation conditions and drafts the rationale, while calculated figures populate the proposal in the {DOCS}. The {WORKFLOW} records funding approval before a validated budget import reaches the {ERP}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finance data, supplier conditions and recovery priorities were separate. The arithmetic was tractable, but assembling comparable assumptions took bespoke work.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes a reusable cost model, quotation extractor and import validator cheaper to build. Existing budget exports and approval features can handle much of the flow.
tasks.still_hard: Recovery benefits are uncertain and often cannot be reduced to a reliable financial return. Supplier pricing, internal capacity and competing funding demands still require human confirmation.
tasks.human_edge: The planner explains which recovery capability a spending choice buys and makes residual exposure understandable to decision makers.
tasks.altitude: Less time goes into reconciling tables and rewriting proposals. The planner can recommend reallocations between recovery options; spending authority remains with the budget holder.

reach.task: Compare investment options under uncertain operational benefits.
reach.learn: Sensitivity analysis, option appraisal and the limits of loss estimates.

reach.task: Plan shared spending on alternate workplaces and emergency supplies.
reach.learn: Capacity costing, renewal commitments and facilities budget cycles.

evidence.claim: Cost scenarios, sensitivity calculations and budget import validation can use deterministic rules.
Continuity investment priorities require judgement about affordability, recovery needs and residual exposure.

assumptions: The pilot covers one budget cycle, one finance export and a limited recovery-option catalogue.
Supplier quotations are already obtained; procurement negotiations are outside these estimates.
Contingency allowances and financial assumptions are explicit human inputs.
The final budget import is available through existing configuration; otherwise a deterministic connector is needed.
Consent and access include finance permissions and any applicable consultation under national rules.
GDPR applies if staffing estimates contain personal data; use aggregate role costs where sufficient.
unknowns: Can the planner obtain approved expenditure and commitment exports?
Which cost allocation, tax and accounting rules must the model follow?
Who can approve funding and accept unfunded recovery requirements?
Does the finance environment support validated budget imports?
research_questions: Which assumptions materially change the ranking of recovery investments?
Which quotation fields can move to structured submissions without shifting excessive work to service owners?
new_work: Review quotation exclusions and ambiguous cost units.
Maintain cost mappings, scenario formulas and import rules.
Refresh expired prices and capacity assumptions.
Investigate failed imports and differences from approved totals.

tasks.short: Develop realistic disruption scenarios and workable sequences for restoring operations.

steps.what: Review impact assessments, incidents, dependencies and existing recovery plans.
Map outage duration, capacity constraints and dependencies against recovery requirements.
Choose credible disruption conditions and recovery options with service owners.
Write scenario timelines, recovery sequences and exercise prompts.

loop.input: Chosen parameters, validated constraints, recovery options and exercise templates.
loop.output: Scenario narratives, event prompts and proposed recovery sequences.
loop.check: Check timings and dependencies deterministically; distinguish exercise fiction from factual capabilities and flag unsupported assumptions.
loop.stop: Generate at most three variants and one correction pass; infeasible or unsupported variants return to the planner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates generate structure, but coherent narratives and prompts must combine varied disruption conditions.

steps.what: Challenge feasibility and approve scenarios for the intended exercise.
Publish the approved scenario pack with controlled access and version details.
Record unresolved capability gaps and assign follow-up work.

tasks.design: A deterministic constraint model on the {DATA_PLATFORM} combines approved dependencies, recovery targets and capacity assumptions from the {DOCS} and structured exports. A bounded loop turns chosen conditions into scenario packs, with calculated timings inserted by code. Service owners approve suitability before the {WORKFLOW} publishes the pack and creates follow-up actions in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Source plans were fragmented and scenario writing was bespoke. Organisations also lacked reliable capacity and dependency data for automatic feasibility checks.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes small constraint models and reusable pack generators practical. Bounded drafting can vary narratives while keeping factual capability claims tied to approved inputs.
tasks.still_hard: Unknown dependencies and correlated failures limit the model. A plausible narrative does not prove that recovery will succeed, and restoration durations need operational evidence.
tasks.human_edge: The planner chooses disruptions that expose meaningful weaknesses and challenges reassuring assumptions without making the exercise pointless.

ambition.what: Compound-disruption exercise packs for small service teams

tasks.altitude: The planner spends less time assembling packs and more time testing assumptions with operators. They can propose a broader exercise programme; service owners retain authority over feasibility claims and exercise participation.

reach.task: Model recovery options when sites, carriers or suppliers become unavailable.
reach.learn: Capacity bottlenecks, lead-time distributions and dependency propagation.

reach.task: Map restoration prerequisites between applications and infrastructure.
reach.learn: Service dependencies, data consistency and evidence from restoration tests.

evidence.claim: Dependency, timing and capacity constraints can be checked with deterministic models when inputs are explicit.
Generated scenario narratives require operational review and do not validate recovery capabilities.

assumptions: The pilot uses a bounded set of critical services and tabletop scenarios.
Recovery targets and capacity estimates remain supplied or validated by service owners.
The automation prior is reduced because scenario credibility and feasibility remain substantial human work.
Build estimates exclude live failover tooling and full operational simulation.
Consent and access cover sensitive plan permissions and any exercise-related consultation required by national rules.
GDPR applies to personal data in incident records; EU AI Act obligations depend on intended use.
unknowns: How current and complete are dependency and capacity records?
Which restoration durations have been tested rather than estimated?
Who may approve scenarios involving multiple services?
Which scenario details must remain restricted before an exercise?
research_questions: Which compound failures reveal gaps that single-service exercises miss?
How well do calculated recovery sequences match observed exercise results?
Which scenario elements need narrative generation rather than parameterised templates?
new_work: Review generated narratives for unsupported capability claims.
Maintain constraint rules, scenario templates and capacity assumptions.
Compare model assumptions with exercise observations.
Manage scenario access and retire obsolete packs.

tasks.short: Interpret applicable regulations and translate them into continuity obligations and controls.

steps.what: Retrieve relevant regulatory publications and check for changes.
Read changed clauses and prepare a referenced obligation summary.

loop.input: Versioned official texts, previous versions and recorded organisational scope.
loop.output: Candidate obligations with exact citations, dates, scope conditions and uncertainty flags.
loop.check: Verify quotations and references against stored text; distinguish binding text from guidance and proposals.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per changed text; missing or conflicting sources go to legal counsel.
loop.why_not_simpler: Change detection is deterministic, but legal duties and exceptions are expressed across prose and cross-references.

steps.what: Determine applicability and approve interpretations with the continuity planner.
Compare approved obligations with current plans, controls and supporting evidence.

loop.input: Approved obligations, versioned controls, continuity plans and evidence references.
loop.output: Proposed obligation-to-control mappings and potential evidence gaps.
loop.check: Require source references for mappings; distinguish missing evidence from demonstrated noncompliance.
loop.stop: One mapping and one correction pass per obligation batch; ambiguous matches require planner review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Identifiers handle established mappings, but new obligations and controls often use different language.

steps.what: Agree corrective actions, owners and deadlines for confirmed gaps.
Update the obligation register and assign approved corrective actions.
Notify affected owners of approved obligations, actions and review dates.

tasks.design: A scheduled job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} checks approved sources in the {GOV_PORTAL} and stores versioned texts in the {DOCS}. Bounded extraction and control-mapping loops produce referenced drafts for legal and operational review. Approved interpretations populate a register in the {WORKFLOW}, which assigns actions in the {PROJECT} and sends notices through the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reliable applicability depended on organisational context, cross-references and professional interpretation. Source monitoring alone could not establish what the organisation needed to change.
tasks.enabler_now: Version comparison, source capture and approval registers are established techniques that are cheaper to assemble with AI-assisted coding. Bounded extraction reduces reading effort when citations are checked against the actual text.
tasks.still_hard: Sector, entity, jurisdiction and implementation details change applicability. Guidance can be ambiguous, and source coverage must be maintained.
tasks.human_edge: The planner connects legal interpretation to practical recovery controls and knows when an apparent compliance gap needs specialist advice.

ambition.what: Continuity obligation briefings for site supervisors

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from searching and copying clauses to testing applicability and resolving control gaps. The planner gains capacity to advise operational owners; legal interpretation and risk acceptance remain with authorised roles.

reach.task: Map obligations to controlled procedures and evidence.
reach.learn: Evidence sufficiency, corrective-action closure and procedure change control.

reach.task: Translate site obligations into emergency and recovery procedures.
reach.learn: Site-specific requirements, inspection evidence and operational constraints.

evidence.claim: Source monitoring, version comparison and obligation registers can use deterministic technology.
Applicability assessment needs organisational context and legal judgement beyond text extraction.
A government report containing nonexistent sources led to a partial refund.

assumptions: The pilot covers an approved, limited set of official sources and one organisational scope.
Legal counsel is available for material or ambiguous interpretations.
The register records evidence gaps separately from confirmed noncompliance.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply as relevant; national rules determine employment and consultation requirements.
Consent and access include legal-document permissions, source access and any required employee consultation.
Build estimates do not include a comprehensive regulatory content subscription or coverage of every jurisdiction.
unknowns: Which entities, countries, sectors and contractual obligations are in scope?
Which official sources and existing interpretations are authoritative?
Who may approve routine interpretations and which issues require external advice?
What employee consultation requirements apply under national rules or existing agreements?
research_questions: Which approved sources provide reliable change feeds or stable version identifiers?
Can reviewers consistently distinguish a missing document from an actual control failure?
What level of source context is needed to avoid losing exceptions and cross-references?
new_work: Maintain source coverage, organisational scope and interpretation review dates.
Check extracted citations, exceptions and effective dates.
Resolve ambiguous mappings and conflicting legal interpretations.
Repair changed source connections and monitor missed publications.

role.altitude: The continuity planner spends more time challenging recovery assumptions, negotiating shared capacity and testing readiness. Better preparation supports more frequent recommendations; funding, legal interpretation, risk acceptance and incident command remain explicit decision rights.
reach: Information technology project management: sequence restoration dependencies and validate recovery evidence.
Facilities management: assess alternate-site capacity and fallback communications.
Management analysis: compare recovery investments under uncertain benefits.
Quality control systems management: connect obligations, procedures and evidence.
skills_to_grow: Recovery cost modelling and sensitivity analysis
Data access, version control and workflow configuration
role.ambitious_version: Provide a rolling recovery-options service that connects investment choices, dependency conflicts and exercise evidence. Use it to bring specific readiness decisions to authorised leaders throughout the year.
